Definition: from G2596 and G515; to deem entirely deserving:--(ac-)count worthy.
BiblicalUsage: To be counted worthy is to be deemed deserving, and those who attain the resurrection are counted worthy, and the apostles rejoiced that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for His name, and Paul prays the Thessalonians may be counted worthy of the kingdom of God. The word holds the honour and the suffering together: worthiness is given by God and proved in the bearing of shame.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe worthiness is not earned but given, and the proof of it is joy in suffering for His name. I hold that the kingdom is worth the shame, and the One who counts me worthy will keep me to the end.
